questions.q: Ethanol (in excess) is heated with conc. H₂SO₄ at 413 K. The main organic product is:
questions.explain: At 413 K with excess ethanol, a second alcohol molecule attacks the protonated alcohol (SN2) to give ethoxyethane; elimination to ethene needs 443 K.

questions.q: The major product of acid-catalysed dehydration of butan-2-ol is:
questions.explain: By Saytzeff's rule the more substituted alkene forms, mostly as the trans (E) isomer; but-1-ene is the minor product.

questions.q: 1-Cyclopentylethanol is heated with conc. H₃PO₄. The major alkene is:
questions.explain: The secondary cation next to the ring undergoes a ring-expanding alkyl shift and then a hydride shift to the tertiary 1-methylcyclohexyl cation, which loses H⁺. Ethylidenecyclopentane is the product only when no carbocation forms (POCl₃/pyridine).

questions.q: Which reagent dehydrates 1-cyclopentylethanol to ethylidenecyclopentane without any rearrangement of the carbon skeleton?
questions.explain: POCl₃ turns –OH into a –OPOCl₂ leaving group and pyridine removes a β-H in one E2 step, so no carbocation and no shift occurs. Acid gives ring expansion, and ThO₂ gives the terminal alkene vinylcyclopentane.
